Flytower 1.4.1 is a security update, and everyone should install it. It comes out of a full review of the code. It tightens how the panel, the system helper and your servers are kept apart, and the checks behind signing in and permissions. Nothing you use day to day changes.

Each Minecraft server now runs in its own group and can no longer see the system helper or the panel's own data. Servers pick this up the next time they restart. The panel is more careful with files in server folders, which the server itself can change. The system helper keeps its own files where only root can change them, and moves older ones across by itself the first time it starts. Updates run one at a time, and **Install** won't go to an older version, though **Go back to** still can. If an update can't save a copy of the database first, it stops and leaves everything as it was. A rollback now only removes files that the new version made.

Sign-in and permissions are stricter too. Discord role mappings and cancelling invites follow the same "no more than you have" rule as roles. Deleting an export or a past world asks for your passkey. Removing a passkey signs out your other devices. Recovery codes and setup tokens are harder to guess. The panel refuses changes that come from other websites. Recovery codes made before 1.4.1 still work, but it's worth making new ones under **Account**. Testing notes are in [testing-1.4.0.md](https://github.com/MattA-Official/mc-panel/blob/v1.4.1/docs/testing/testing-1.4.0.md).
